summary: npx inngest-cli@latest dev fails in this sandboxed shell unless install scripts are explicitly allowed
details: The harness blocks npm postinstall scripts by default (visible via 'npm warn install-scripts ... not covered by allowScripts'). inngest-cli's postinstall fetches its platform binary, so a bare `npx inngest-cli@latest dev` fails with 'Error: Inngest CLI binary not found' in this environment even though `INNGEST_DEV=1` and the /api/inngest route are wired correctly. Verified the wiring by temporarily adding inngest-cli as a devDependency, running `npm install-scripts approve inngest-cli` + `npm rebuild inngest-cli`, then running the locally-installed binary directly (./node_modules/.bin/inngest dev -u http://localhost:3000/api/inngest) — this synced the post-forge app with functionCount: 0 as expected. Removed the temporary devDependency afterward so package.json matches the BRD's npx-based workflow.
proposedAction: When T16 (or any human) runs `npx inngest-cli@latest dev` locally outside this sandbox, it should work normally since real environments don't block install scripts. If verifying again inside a similarly sandboxed agent shell, use `npm install -D inngest-cli && npm install-scripts approve inngest-cli && npm rebuild inngest-cli` and run the local binary instead of npx.
